title: Structured Response Integrity Testbed for Low-Precision Serving
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Objective: build an automated, reproducible testbed that measures structured-output (JSON/function-call) fidelity when we serve models in low-precision modes (FP8 and INT8) and tie those regressions to actionable calibration and rollout decisions.

Background: recent quant profiles improve throughput but we've observed non-linear schema failures for nested function-call outputs under certain tokenization edgecases and truncated KV cache states. Existing test harnesses target token-level perplexity and generation metrics; we need a focused, deterministic suite that asserts JSON schema adherence, field-level type fidelity, and deterministic enum/ordinal outputs across calibration variants.

This ticket scopes the infra and test definitions (datasets, fuzzers, baselines) and a small automation loop that gates model rollout in the Canary pipeline by structured-output pass rates and targeted regression detectors.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible test harness exists in ci/structured-integrity with a single command to run FP32, FP8, and INT8 variants and emit a JSON report.
Schema-failure delta: For the canonical function-calling benchmark set, FP8 and INT8 run results must not exceed +0.5% absolute schema-failure rate over FP32 baseline for P1 rollout approval.
Per-field type error rates broken out by schema path and quant config are included in the report (e.g., $.response.items[*].id : type mismatch count).
Nightly CI job executes the suite and posts artifacts to the artifacts bucket with a permalink; failing runs create a Jira/Linear ticket automatically with sample failing prompts and model seed.
Integration tests include a set of synthetic fuzzed payloads that reproduce at least 3 real customer regressions from the last 6 months (anonymized).
test_plan: Datasets: combine 3 corpora — function-call telemetry corpus (internal), developer-supplied prompt sets (anonymized), and synthetic generators for deeply nested objects.
Prompts: canonical set (500 prompts) plus 10k fuzzed variations using byte-level token mutation, whitespace permutations, and unexpected enum values.
Baseline: run models in FP32 and record per-prompt golden outputs and schema parse trees. Compare low-precision runs against this baseline with deterministic seeds.
Metrics: schema_fail_rate, field_type_error_rate, enum_mismatch_rate, average_structural_edit_distance, example_count_of_reproducible_failures.
Automation: GitHub Actions workflow 'quant-structured-integrity.yml' runs on PRs modifying calibration/quant profiles and nightly against release candidates.
calibration_workflow_changes: We will add a calibration validation step post-collect that runs the structured-integrity harness at each candidate quant profile commit. Calibration pipelines must persist calibration metadata (scale factors, outlier stats) and produce a calibration_signature used by the test harness to correlate failures. If structural regressions exceed thresholds, calibration artifacts are flagged and a rollback marker is created in the model registry.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Experimental: run testbed on dedicated staging pool with synthetic workload; require manual approval for any quant profile with >0 failures.
Phase 2 - Canary: integrate harness into canary gating for 5% traffic; if nightly structural delta >0.25% open rollback workflow and halt further rollout.
Phase 3 - General availability: once 14-day rolling window shows stable metrics under thresholds, mark profile GA and update runtime recommendation docs.
monitoring: Dashboard: structured_integrity/model/{model_name}/profile/{quant} showing schema_fail_rate (7d/24h), top-10 failing schema paths, and example prompt IDs.
Alert: PagerDuty if schema_fail_rate for a production profile increases by >0.5 percentage points within 1h and absolute rate >1%.
Logs: attach example payloads, model seed, calibration_signature, and KV cache state snapshot to error events for triage.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Some schema failures are brittle to non-deterministic sampling and beam search differences after quantization. Mitigation: use deterministic decoding in CI runs and include beam/temperature variations as separate axes.
Risk: Running the full suite is expensive. Mitigation: implement stratified sampling and a fast smoke check (50 prompts) for PR-level feedback, full run nightly.

Risk: False positives because baselines include previously tolerated minor format drifts. Mitigation: add a historical-tolerance parameter and allow per-field grace thresholds configurable per project.
